verdict_text:
YES

The script correctly casts exactly the 64 named projection matrices to bfloat16 via `float().to(bfloat16)`, upcasts every other retained tensor to float32, and deletes exactly the 48 named buffers via `buffer_re` scoped to per-layer attention bias/masked_bias/rotary inv_freq (not matching embed_in/embed_out or top-level norms). It asserts the four required checks (64 bfloat16 tensors, layer-0 QKV weight is bfloat16, embed_in.weight is float32, total 196 tensors) before writing, satisfying "fail loudly." The shard-packing logic isolates any tensor whose size alone exceeds `max_bytes` into its own shard (the `cur and cur_size+size>max_bytes` check triggers regardless of `cur`'s prior contents when the new tensor alone exceeds the cap), which correctly handles embed_in/embed_out once upcast to float32 (~412MB > 256MiB). The index file's `weight_map` covers every tensor, and names are left unchanged throughout.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm). verdict none = no answer, excluded from rates.
